title: Typed Arrays and Function Contracts
summary: Use typed arrays, tuples, parameter and return types, optional/default parameters, callbacks, and overload-free union contracts.
learningObjectives: Explain and apply the TypeScript behavior taught in Typed Arrays and Function Contracts
Use strict compiler evidence and runtime tests to verify the contract
prerequisiteConcepts: Ability to create and save a text file

sections.heading: Core model
sections.content: An array type such as `number[]` constrains every element, while a tuple records a fixed sequence of positions with distinct types. Function parameter types protect callers and explicit return types protect the implementation's contract. Optional parameters come after required ones; default parameters already behave as optional to callers. Callback types describe both inputs and outputs, enabling methods such as `map` to infer results. Prefer a union parameter when behavior and return type are the same for every member; overloads are useful only when input forms imply meaningfully different output types.
keyPoints: An array type such as `number[]` constrains every element, while a tuple records a fixed sequence of positions with distinct types.
commonMistakes: optional does not mean every value type is accepted
readonly is compile-time protection, not deep runtime freezing

sections.heading: Guided practice
sections.content:
1. Add the example to a strict TypeScript project.
2. Predict inferred types.
3. Run `tsc --noEmit`.
4. Introduce one mismatch and read the diagnostic.
5. Correct the contract without `any`.
6. Run the JavaScript and record evidence.
